blocks.text: The census measured 638 of 1006 tables in scope, reading 5.9m rows in 15.5 minutes. Of those, 513 had a complete pass and the others were measured by sample. 44 tables failed. The result receipt is digest-verified and the ledger records admit, gate and converge.

The delivery is partial. Only 3 of 6 connections completed, 2 are partial and 1 is blocked: artists_app was refused access, and the grant is an owner dependency. We recommend accepting the census as a documented partial record while keeping the commission open until artists_app is read and the failed tables are re-run. Several counts in the report do not reconcile with one another; they are disclosed here rather than repaired.

The exhibit splits tables by method: complete pass, stratified sample, head sample, failed and not reached. Complete passes are the largest group, so most of the measured evidence is firm. The remainder is either estimated from part of a table or absent.

The categories in the exhibit do not reconcile with the tables in scope, and the method counts 513, 83 and 41 do not reconcile exactly with 638. We have kept the values as supplied and drawn no coverage percentage from them.

blocks.caption: The method counts show how firm each part of the evidence is; they do not reconcile to the headline totals, so no coverage percentage should be taken from them.

blocks.text: 638 of 1006 tables were measured. 513 had a complete pass, 83 were stratified samples and 41 were head samples. A complete pass gives whole-table figures; a sample gives ratios drawn from part of the table.

Measured therefore does not mean exhaustively read. For anything that depends on exact ratios, treat the sampled tables as indicative until a complete pass is run. Percentage shares of coverage are not quoted here because the totals behind them need validating.

sections.heading: Coverage of the tables in scope

blocks.text: 44 tables failed because the worker could not measure them in this run. The recorded errors are the route to closing them. The work that was done is documented: 5.9m rows read and 351.3 GiB of data and index measured.

259.3m rows held is an estimate of what the estate contains and must not be added to the measured rows. The 15.5 minutes of wall clock describes this run only. It is not a guarantee of future speed and not a charge.

sections.heading: What failed, and what was read

blocks.text: Coverage is uneven. 3 connections are complete, 2 are partial and 1 is blocked, and the blocked connection, artists_app, contributes no tables.
The series is labelled as tables measured but sums to the tables in scope rather than to 638. Its label needs clarifying, and its total should not be used as a validated measured-table count.

blocks.caption: The series sums to the tables in scope, not to the tables measured, so its measured label needs clarifying; the blocked connection shows no tables.

blocks.text: Measured data and index volume is heavily concentrated in iebc_forms; the other connections together hold a small remainder. The aggregate of 351.3 GiB gives the context.
The zero shown for artists_app is a consequence of denied access, not evidence that it holds no data. Footprint should be read as what was measured, not as the size of the estate.

blocks.text: 3 of 6 connections completed, 2 are partial and 1 is blocked, with 20 databases measured. artists_app was refused access by the database; the grant is pending and sits with the owner. citizen_digital and citizen-pulse reached tables but had failures.

Accepting this delivery as complete would accept all of that unresolved coverage. Reading artists_app alone would not repair the partial connections or the failed tables, so the re-census needs to cover all three.

The ledger holds 3 rows for the run, recording admit, gate and converge. The lawful basis admit limits the scope to census only. The report states that it holds aggregates, sketches and hashes, and we attribute that statement to the report rather than treating it as independently verified.

The executive dossier used 17679 tokens in and 4583 tokens out. Object-storage enumeration is a separate run with its own receipt: it reached 106 buckets and 40 were unreachable. Ledger success and receipt integrity do not show that every table was fully read.

First, accept the census as a partial record, resting on 638 of 1006 tables, and keep the commission open. Second, grant access to artists_app so it can be re-censused; this is the only blocker that depends on you.

Third, have the errors behind the 44 failed tables addressed and re-run them with the partial connections. Fourth, order complete passes where sampled ratios matter, covering 83 stratified and 41 head-sampled tables. Finally, ask for the unreconciled counts, the series label and the missing references to be clarified before any percentage is quoted.

sections.heading: What to do first, and why

blocks.text: Any downstream decision is bounded by 638 against 1006. Failed and unreached tables tell us nothing either way, and ratios on sampled tables are not whole-table measurements. A complete-pass census on those tables would close this gap.

Languages, rights and semantic similarity were not measured. Closing them needs rights declared at source and a language and similarity pass. Digest verification and a successful ledger confirm the integrity of what was delivered; they do not remove any of these limits.
